filename: EcoPro-LSTMv0_ A Memory-based Machine Learning Approach to Predicting Ecosystem Dynamics across Time Scales in Mediterranean Environments(1).pdf
title: EcoPro-LSTMv0: A Memory-based Machine Learning Approach to Predicting Ecosystem Dynamics across Time Scales in Mediterranean Environments
testbed_rationale: Provides a reproducible benchmark combining multi-timescale FLUXNET2015 tower data for simultaneously predicting coupled terrestrial water and carbon fluxes (GPP, RECO, ET, SWC) with code and tutorial publicly available.
pain_points: High computational cost in training time and memory (18 GB RAM, 16 CPU cores) limiting data scaling on CPUs
Data sparsity and missing records (multiple sites excluded due to lack of soil moisture data or <1 year of data)
Suboptimal observational data quality and noise for certain sites (e.g. AU-Rig, ES-LJu)
Collinearity among meteorological drivers creating challenges for feature attribution methods like SHAP
Sensitivity of Integrated Gradients (IG) to the selection of the baseline neutral state
Equifinality where multiple ML models explain observational data equally well without resolving underlying physical interactions
extraction_notes: EcoPro-LSTMv0 uses a multi-timescale dual-input sequence (120-day daily memory and 3-day hourly memory) trained in a multi-task learning configuration to predict carbon and water cycle fluxes across Mediterranean sites.
